questions.q: The fractional change in the magnetic field intensity at a distance $r$~from centre on the axis of current carrying coil of radius $a$~to the magnetic field intensity at the centre of the same coil is: (Take $r < a$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know,

${B}_{axis} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}{iR}^{2}}{2\left(R^{2} + x^{2}\right)3 / 2}\text{where}, R = a$~

${B}_{centre } = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{2a}$

$∴ {B}_{axis } = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}{ia}^{2}}{2\left(a^{2} + r^{2}\right)3 / 2}$

$∴$ fractional change in magnetic field $= \dfrac{\dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{2a} - \dfrac{{μ}_{0}ia^{2}}{2\left(a^{2} + r^{2}\right)3 / 2}}{{μ}_{0}i2a} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{\left[1 + \left(\dfrac{r2}{a2}\right)\right]3 / 2}$

$\approx 1 - \left[1 - \dfrac{3}{2}\dfrac{r2}{a2}\right] = \dfrac{3}{2}\dfrac{r2}{a2}$

questions.q: A particle of mass $m$ and charge $q$ is in an electric and magnetic field given by $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}}=$2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j} ; $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}}=$4 \hat{j}+6 \hat{k} The charged particle is shifted from the origin to the point $\mathrm{P}(x=1 ; y=1)$ along a straight path. The magnitude of the total work done is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Resultant force on the charged particle
=$\overrightarrow{F}_{net }=$q $\overrightarrow{E}+$q($\overrightarrow{V} \times \overrightarrow{B})$
=(2 q \hat{i}+3 q \hat{j})+q($\overrightarrow{v} \times \overrightarrow{B})$
Also $\mathrm{q}(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{V}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}})=0$ So, required work done $\begin{aligned} \mathrm{W}$&=$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}}_{\mathrm{net}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{S}}=($2 $\mathrm{q} \hat{\mathrm{i}}+$3 $\mathrm{q} \hat{\mathrm{j}}) \cdot(\hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{j}})$\\ &=2 $\mathrm{q}+$3 $\mathrm{q}$\\ &=5 $\mathrm{q} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: Two long straight wires $P$~and $Q$ carrying equal current $10A$ each were kept parallel to each other at $5$ cm distance. Magnitude of magnetic force experienced by $10$ cm length of wire $P$ is ${F}_{1}$. If distance between wires is halved and currents on them are doubled, force ${F}_{2}$~on $10$ cm length of wire $P$ will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know, force per unit length between two parallel straight wires is given by, $F = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}{i}_{1}{i}_{2}}{2\pid}$.

Therefore, required ratio

$\dfrac{F1}{{F}_{2}} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0} ( 10{)}^{2}2\pi ( 5 \times {10}^{- 2} )}{{μ}_{0} ( 20{)}^{2}2\pi\left(\dfrac{5}{2} \times {10}^{- 2}\right)} = \dfrac{1}{8}$

$⇒ {F}_{2} = 8{F}_{1}$

questions.q: Two bar magnets oscillate in a horizontal plane in earth's magnetic field with time periods of $3s$~and $4s$respectively. If their moments of inertia are in the ratio of $3: 2$& then the ratio of their magnetic moments will be&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Torque on a bar magnet kept in a magnetic field is given by& $τ = MBsin\theta$.

Hence, for small oscillations the time period of bar magnets is given by,

$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{I}{MB}} ⇒ M ∝ \dfrac{I}{T2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{M1}{M2} = \dfrac{I1}{I2} \times \left(\dfrac{T2}{T1}\right)2$

$⇒ \dfrac{M1}{M2} = \dfrac{3}{2} \times \left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)2 = \dfrac{8}{3}$

The distances from the centre of the wire's cross-section at which the magnetic field [inside the wire, outside the wire] is half of the maximum possible magnetic field, any where due to the wire, will be
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q: An electron is constrained to move along the $y$-axis with a speed of $0 . 1c$ (c is the speed of light) in the presence of electromagnetic wave, whose electric field is $\overset{→}{E} = 30\overset{^}{j}sin\left(1 . 5 \times {10}^{7}t - 5 \times {10}^{- 2}x\right)Vm^{- 1} .$~where $t$~in in seconds and~$x$~is im meters.The maximum magnetic force experienced by the electron will be: (given $c = 3 \times {10}^{8}ms^{- 1}$ and electron charge $= 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}Coloumbs$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In electromagnetic wave is $\dfrac{E0}{B0} = C$
so maximum value of magnetic field is

${B}_{0} = \dfrac{E0}{C}$

${F}_\max = qV{B}_\max \cdot sin90 °$

$= \dfrac{q{V}_{0}{E}_{0}}{C}N$

$\dfrac{1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19} \times 0 . 1 \times 3 \times {10}^{8} \times 30}{3 \times {10}^{8}} = 4 . 8 \times {10}^{- 19}N$

questions.q: A rigid wire consists of a semicircular portion of radius $R$ and two straight sections. The wire is partially immerged in a perpendicular magnetic field $B = {B}_{0}\overset{^}{j}$ as shown in figure. The magnetic force on the wire if it has a current $i$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Direction of magnetic field is in $+ \overset{^}{k}$

Force acting on wire is given by, $\overset{→}{F} = i \left(\overset{→}{l} \times \overset{→}{B}\right)

As, $l = 2R$, we get

$⇒ \overset{→}{F} = - 2iRB\overset{^}{j}$

$

questions.q: A bar magnet having a magnetic moment of $2 . 0 \times {10}^{5}JT^{- 1}$, is placed along the direction of uniform magnetic field of magnitude $B = 14 \times {10}^{- 5}T$. The work done in rotating the magnet slowly through $60 °$ from the direction of field is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Work done by the external force is equal to the change in the potential energy,

${W}_{ext} = \Delta U = {U}_{f} - {U}_{i}$

$⇒ {W}_{ext} = - MBcos{θ}_{2} + MBcos{θ}_{1}$

$⇒ {W}_{ext} = MB \left(cos{θ}_{1} - cos{θ}_{2}\right)$

$⇒ {W}_{ext} = 14 \times {10}^{- 5} \times2 \times {10}^{5} \left(cos0 ° - cos60 °\right)$

$⇒ {W}_{ext} = 14 \times 2 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 14J$

questions.q:
A coil is placed in magnetic field such that plane of coil is perpendicular to the direction of magnetic field. The magnetic flux through a coil can be changed:

A. By changing the magnitude of the magnetic field within the coil.

B. By changing the area of coil within the magnetic field.

C. By changing the angle between the direction of magnetic field and the plane of the coil.

D. By reversing the magnetic field direction abruptly without changing its magnitude.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Magnetic flux through a coil is given by& $ϕ = \overset{→}{B} . \overset{→}{A}= BAcos\theta$, where,$B$is~magnetic field, $A$~is~area of coil and $\theta$~is~the angle between $B$ and $A$.

Thus, from above expression, we can say that magnetic flux can~be changed by changing magnetic field, area of coil, change the angle between~$B$ and $A$.

Hence, correct& options are A, B and C.

questions.q: An electron gun is placed inside a long solenoid of radius $R$ on its axis. The solenoid has $n$ turns/length and carries a current $I .$ The electron gun shoots an electron along the radius of the solenoid with speed $v .$ If the electron does not hit the surface of the solenoid, maximum possible value of $v$ is (all symbols have their standard meaning):
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Magnetic Field Inside Solenoid is $B = {μ}_{0}nI$

Velocity $ν$~has given~to the electron~

So, Magnetic Force

$F = qνB$

as~$ν$and~$B$~are perpendicular.

In a magnetic field, charge will move on a circular path. Here, If radius is just less than or equal to radius of solenoid then the electron does not hit the surface.

$F = qνB = \dfrac{m{ν}^{2}}{R} ⇒ mν = qBRasq = eν = \dfrac{eBR}{m}So, V = \dfrac{e{μ}_{0}nIR}{m}$

questions.q: A moving coil galvanometer has a coil with $175$ turns and area $1cm^{2} .$ It uses a torsion band of torsion constant ${10}^{- 6}Nm / rad$ The coil is placed in a magnetic field B parallel to its plane. The coil deflects by ${1}^{o}$ for a current of $1mA$ The value of B (in tesla) is approximately:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{ppm}($ parts per million $)=\frac{\mathrm{mg} \text { of solute }}{\mathrm{L} \text { of solution }}$
Given,
$\mathrm{ppm}=1000\begin{aligned} & \text { volume }=1 \mathrm{~L} \\ & \mathrm{mg} \text { of solute }=\mathrm{ppm} \times \mathrm{L} \text { of solution } \\ & =10^3 \times 1 \\ & \text { weight of solute }=10^3 \mathrm{mg}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \text { Concentration }=\frac{\text { no. of moles }}{\text { volume }} \\ & \text { no. of moles }=\frac{\text { weight of solute }}{\text { molecular weight of solute }}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{10^3 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~g}}{100 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}}\left[1 \mathrm{mg}=10^{-3} \mathrm{~g}\right] \\ & =10^{-2} \mathrm{~mol}\end{aligned}$
Concentration (c) $=\frac{10^{-2} \mathrm{~mol}}{1 \mathrm{~L}}=10^{-2} \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1}$

questions.q: A small circular loop of conducting wire has radius a and carries current $I .$ It is placed in a uniform magnetic field $B$ perpendicular to its plane such that when rotated slightly about its diameter and released, it starts performing simple harmonic motion of time period $T .$~The mass of the loop is $m$ then:

questions.solution:
$τ = MBsin ⁡ \theta = I\alpha$
$\piR^{2}iB\theta = \dfrac{mR^{2}}{2}\alpha$
$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{2\piiB}{m}} = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}; T = \sqrt{\dfrac{2\pim}{iB}}$

questions.q: A uniform magnetic field of $2 \times {10}^{- 3}T$ acts along positive Y-direction. A rectangular loop of sides $20$ cm and $10$ cm with current of $5A$ is in Y-Z plane. The current is in anticlockwise sense with reference to negative X axis. Magnitude and direction of the torque is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$

Magnetic moment is given by, $\overset{→}{M} = i\overset{→}{A}$

$= 5 \times \left(0 . 2\right)\times \left($0 . 1\$right)\left(- \overset{^}{i}\right)$

$= 0 . 1 \left(- \overset{^}{i}\right)

$\overset{→}{τ} = \overset{→}{M} $\times \overset{→}{B} =$0 .1 \left(- \overset{^}{i}\right) \times \left($2 $\times {10}^{- 3}\right) \left(\overset{^}{j}\right)$

questions.q:
Uniform magnetic fields of different strengths \left(B_1\right.$ and $B_2$), both normal to the plane of the paper exist as shown in the figure. A charged particle of mass m and charge q , at the interface at an instant, moves into the region 2 with velocity $v$ and returns to the interface. It continues to move into region 1 and finally reaches the interface. What is the displacement of the particle during this movement along the interface?

(Consider the velocity of the particle to be normal to the magnetic field and $B_2 \gt B_1$)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}$ is $\perp$ to $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}}$, so charge particle will move in circular path, whose radius is given by
$\mathrm{R}=\frac{\mathrm{mv}}{\mathrm{qB}}$

Starting point $\rightarrow \mathrm{A}$
Ending point $\rightarrow \mathrm{C}$
$\therefore$ Net displacement $=\mathrm{AC}$
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{AC}=\mathrm{CD}-\mathrm{AD} \\ & \mathrm{AC}=\frac{2 \mathrm{mv}}{\mathrm{qB}_1}-\frac{2 \mathrm{mv}}{\mathrm{qB}_2} \\ & \mathrm{AC}=\frac{2 \mathrm{mv}}{\mathrm{qB}_1}\left[1-\frac{\mathrm{B}_1}{\mathrm{~B}_2}\right]\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The magnetic moments associated with two closely wound circular coils $A$ and $B$ of radius ${r}_{A} = 10cm\text{and}{r}_{B} = 20cm$ respectively are equal if: (Where ${N}_{A}, {I}_{A}\text{and}{N}_{B}, {I}_{B}$ are number of turn and current of $A\text{and}B$ respectively)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As magnetic moment of both the coil is the same,

${μ}_{1} = {μ}_{2}$

$⇒ {N}_{A}\left[{I}_{A}\pi\left({r}_A^{2}\right)\right] = {N}_{B}\left[{I}_{B}\pi\left({r}_B^{2}\right)2\right] ⇒ {N}_{A}\left[{I}_{A}\left(0 . 10\right)2\right] = {N}_{B}\left[{I}_{B}\left(0 . 20\right)2\right] ⇒ {I}_{A}{N}_{A} = 4{I}_{B}{N}_{B}$

questions.q: A triangular shaped wire carrying $10A$ current is placed in a uniform magnetic field of $0 . 5T$, as shown in figure. The magnetic force on segment $CD$ is (Given $BC = CD = BD = 5cm$).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Force due to magnetic field on a current carrying conductor is given by,& $\overset{→}{F} = i\overset{→}{l} \times \overset{→}{B}$.

The angle between the magnetic field and the direction of the current in the wire~$CD$~is~$60 °$. Therefore,

$F = ilBsin60 ° ⇒ F = 10 \times 0 . 05 \times 0 . 5 \times \dfrac{3}{2} ⇒ F = 0 . 216N$

questions.q: A current loop, having two circular arcs joined by two radial lines is shown in the figure. It carries a current of $10A .$ The magnetic field at point $O$ will be close to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Magnetic field due to $PQ$ and $RS$ are zero at ' $O$ '.

Magnetic field due to $QR$

${B}_{QR} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{10}{3 \times {10}^{- 2}}\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ (outwards)

Magnetic field due to $SP$

${B}_{SP} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{10}{5 \times {10}^{- 2}}\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ (inwards)

Net field $B = \dfrac{{\mu}_{o}}{4\pi}\dfrac{10\pi}{4 \times {10}^{- 2}} \left(\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{1}{5}\right)

$= 1.0 $\times {10}^{- 5}$T

questions.q: An electron is projected with uniform velocity along the axis inside a current carrying long solenoid. Then :
options: the electron will continue to move with uniform velocity along the axis of the solenoid.
the electron will be accelerated along the axis.
the electron path will be circular about the axis.
the electron will experience a force at $45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$ to the axis and execute a helical path.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Since $\vec{v} \| \vec{B}$ so force on electron due to magnetic field is zero. So it will move along axis with uniform velocity.

questions.q: A bar magnet with a magnetic moment $5 . 0Am^{2}$ is placed in parallel position relative to a magnetic field of $0 . 4T$. The amount of required work done in turning the magnet form parallel to antiparallel position relative to the field direction is ________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For a bar magnet, the work done in turning from parallel to antiparallel& position relative to the field direction is&

$W = MB \left(cos{θ}_{1} - cos{θ}_{2}\right)$, here,~${θ}_{1} = 0 ° and{θ}_{1} = 180 °$.

$W = - MBcos180 ° \left(-mBcos0 °\right)$

$W = 2MB = 2 \times5 \times0 . 4 = 4J$

questions.q: A straight wire carrying a current of $14A$~is bent into a semicircular arc of radius $2 . 2cm$ as shown in the figure. The magnetic field produced by the current at the centre $O$ of the arc is ____ $\times {10}^{– 4}T$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
It is given that&

$i = 14AR = 2 . 2 \times {10}^{- 2}m$

The magnetic field at the centre~$O$~is

$B = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{4R} = \dfrac{4\pi \times {10}^{- 7} \times 14}{4 \times 2 . 2 \times {10}^{- 2}} = 2 \times {10}^{- 4}T$

questions.q: A charge of $4 . 0\muC$ is moving with a velocity of $4 . 0 \times {10}^{6}ms^{- 1}$ along the positive $y$-axis under a magnetic field $B$ of strength $( 2\overset{^}{k} ) T$. The force acting on the charge is $x\overset{^}{i}N$. The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:

$q = 4\muC, \overset{→}{v} = 4 \times {10}^{6}\overset{^}{j}ms^{- 1}$ and $\overset{→}{B} = 2\overset{^}{k}T$

Force acting on charged particle, $\overset{→}{F} = q ( \overset{→}{v} \times \overset{→}{B} )$

$= 4 \times {10}^{- 6} \left(4 \times {10}^{6}\overset{^}{j} \times2\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$= 4 \times {10}^{- 6} \times8 \times {10}^{6}\overset{^}{i}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{F} = 32\overset{^}{i}N$

$⇒ x = 32

$

Magnitude of the resultant magnetic field at point P at a distance of 4 cm from wire Y is $x \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~T}$. The value of $x$ is__________ . Take permeability of free space as $\mu_0=4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{SI}$ units.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & B=\frac{\mu_0(5)}{2 \pi \times .01}-\frac{\mu_0 4}{2 \pi \times 0.04} \\ & =-\frac{100 \mu_0}{4 \pi} \\ & =-100 \times 10^{-7} \\ & =-1 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~T}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A long solenoid with $1000turnsm^{- 1}$ has a core material with relative permeability $500$ and volume ${10}^{3}{cm}^{3} .$~If the core material is replaced by another material having relative permeability of $750$ with same volume maintaining same current of $0 . 75A$ in the solenoid, the fractional change in the magnetic moment of the core would be approximately \left(\dfrac{x}{499}\right) .$~Find the value of $x .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\overset{→}{M} = \dfrac{magnetic moment \left(\overset{→}{m}\right)}{V}$
$⇒ χ\overset{→}{H} = \overset{→}{m}V$
$⇒ \overset{→}{m} = \left({μ}_{r} - 1\right)NiV$
$∴ \dfrac{\Deltam}{m} = \dfrac{[ \left(750 - 1\right) - \left(500 - 1\right) ] NiV}{\left(500 - 1\right)NiV} = 250$

questions.q: The magnetic potential due to a magnetic dipole at a point on its axis situated at a distance of $20$ cm from its center is $1 . 5 \times {10}^{- 5}Tm$. The magnetic moment of the dipole is _______ $Am^{2}$. (Given : $\dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi} = {10}^{- 7}TmA^{- 1}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the magnetic potential due to a magnetic dipole can be written as

$V = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{M}{r2} . . . \left(1\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) and solve to calculate the required magnetic moment of the dipole.

$1 . 5 \times {10}^{- 5} = {10}^{- 7} \times $\dfrac{M}{\left(20 \times {10}^{- 2}\right)2}$⇒ M = $\dfrac{1 . 5 \times {10}^{- 5} \times 20 \times 20 \times {10}^{- 4}}{10- 7}$⇒ M = 1 . 5 \times4 = 6Am^{2}

$
